title: Special right triangles (45-45-90, 30-60-90) and shapes hiding them
subtitle: Right triangles and trigonometry · 16 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **16 of the official questions in Right triangles and trigonometry are this one** — 0 Easy, 5 Medium, 11 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You see two equal acute angles or two equal legs, a 30° or 60° angle, the words 'isosceles right', 'equilateral', a height or altitude, a square's diagonal, or a square inscribed in a circle.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Name the triangle: equal legs means 45-45-90 with sides x, x, x√2; a 30° or 60° angle, or half of an equilateral triangle, means 30-60-90 with sides x, x√3, 2x.
- 2) Match the given length to the right position in that pattern to find x (the altitude of an equilateral triangle is the x√3 side; the diagonal of a square is the x√2 side).
- 3) Build what's asked (a side, perimeter, area, or angle) from x.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: It mostly can't find the pattern for you.
Its use is checking at the end: type your radical answer and each choice as decimals to match forms like 6√2 against 12/√2.
If the problem gives a perimeter, you can also solve x + x√3 + 2x = P by graphing.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You put the given length in the wrong slot, for example treating the hypotenuse of a 45-45-90 as a leg (multiplying by √2 instead of dividing), or treating an equilateral triangle's height as a full side.
On perimeter or area questions you stop after finding one side.
